model_annotation: Figure 4 is a donut chart illustrating the distribution of samples (as percentages) across different levels of sample-level ambiguity, categorized by two metrics: ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer),” is divided into four segments: Std: 0.0 (18.0%, dark blue), Std: 0.47 (47.7%, medium blue), Std: 0.82 (19.0%, light blue), and Std: 0.94 (14.2%, very light blue). The inner ring, labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner),” contains three segments: Max: 1 (38.0%, medium blue), Max: 2 (19.0%, light blue), and Max: 3 (14.2%, very light blue). The chart uses a color-coded legend to associate each segment with its corresponding ambiguity level, and the percentages are displayed directly within each segment. The visual layout suggests that the outer ring represents a finer granularity of ambiguity variation, while the inner ring groups samples by their peak ambiguity value.
